chunks: And it was narrated from him, عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, that he said:
"Whoever brings a sacrificial animal during an Umrah, then he should slaughter it before shaving his head."

He said: "And whoever brings a sacrificial animal while he is performing Umrah, he slaughters his sacrificial animal at the place of slaughter, and it is between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and it is al-Hazwarah."

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two well-known ritual points of sa'y
key_terms.الْحَزْوَرَةُ: al-Hazwarah, the location identified here with the place of slaughter
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other ritual point paired with al-Safa
key_terms.عُمْرَةٍ: the minor pilgrimage performed at the Sacred House
key_terms.فَلْيَنْحَرْ: let him slaughter; an instruction to perform ritual slaughter
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial animal brought along for offering during the rites
key_terms.يَحْلِقَ: to shave, referring here to shaving the head as part of the rite

ai.seo_question: Where should a person performing Umrah slaughter a sacrificial animal, and should it be done before shaving the head?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the one performing Umrah who has brought a sacrificial animal. It states that the sacrificial animal is to be slaughtered before shaving the head, and it identifies the manhar as being between al-Safa and al-Marwah at al-Hazwarah.
